title: Your projects stop being alone
summary: A brain could already read its siblings; now it can address them. Peer mail asks a connected project a question and gets an answer reasoned from its own code, and the Meeting Room — its own window now, one answer per agent — puts one announcement in front of every agent you have. Lab answers with a report rather than a number, or with a small multi-page app its own script writes. And chat retired its fixed chart types for HTML the agent writes itself, in a sandbox wearing the app's own theme.

title: The conversation grows a cockpit
summary: The chat composer is rebuilt end to end. Modes become real behaviour — Basic, Plan (interviews you, ends by creating a task), Develop (implements in waves, with evidence) — and the same menu carries a never-escalating permission posture. Model and reasoning effort share one trigger with an effort slider and a set-as-default. The session pins what it knows above where you type: the exact git checkout it acts on, agent-pinned facts that stay put, and task progress read from the acceptance criteria themselves. Plus a usage ring fed by Claude Code's own limits cache, closed tabs that finally reap their claude processes, and four silent-failure fixes — a vault that lost its own history to doctor, migrations that never fired on the desktop app's first run, an update that could not report a no-op, and a task sync that stripped local-only fields.

title: Every project you have open, awake in one window
summary: The desktop app stops being one window per project. Everything you have open lives in a single chip strip, every one of them still running, and each chip says what its agent is doing — working, blocked and waiting on you, or something you haven't seen yet — so a question from a project you aren't looking at reaches you instead of sitting there. Picking a project moved to ⌥Tab so Control chords stay with the terminal. Automations gained a shape you can read, ask their questions in the conversation you are already having, and can deliver a finished run's result to your phone.

title: It keeps its own hours, and travels a third as heavy
summary: Two releases in one upgrade — v0.22.0 was built but never reached anyone, so Automations arrives here alongside the snapshot rework. Give the brain a job on a schedule and leave it alone: a headless Claude run that learns from every run, replays the session it had, and tells you what it actually found. And when you do sit down together, everything it knows loads in 16,320 characters instead of 48,964 — each person with their own constitution, the soul keeping only what is unconditionally true, and the conditional rules moved into patterns that can never be demoted into silence.

title: Your agent, as an app — Chat is the screen every session opens in
summary: The in-app agent stops being a terminal: a native 12-state Chat screen where questions become clickable cards, tool calls become collapsible cards, and boards, images and video render in place. It is now the default screen for every Claude session, with the embedded TUI still one dropdown away as Terminal (legacy). What's New also became a release history — one page per version, built from real screenshots.

title: The brain starts forming opinions — falsifiable theses, re-tested every sleep cycle
summary: The proactive learning layer lands: claims your project makes about itself, with predictions registered before the evidence arrives, a cited evidence ledger, and a confidence derived by arithmetic rather than felt. Alongside it, funnel analytics in Lab — and What's New itself. The 0.20.1 patch on top of it made task sync survive a full-size backend.

title: Every task gets its own Claude — and goal-skill takes the build the whole way
summary: Open a task and a dedicated Claude Code session is pinned inside the task view, maintaining the document rather than implementing it. The goal orchestrator was rewritten around it — builders fork and resume, judges stay clean — plus a live agent dock, sleep that stopped duplicating knowledge, and one-click delegation from the board.
